MINUTES
  Regular Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  February 9, 2026
  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:13 p.m., on Monday, February 9, 2026, the Alhambra City Council met in the
Council Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  LEE, MAZA, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Hembree, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director
of Finance Lieu, Director of Community Development Ho, Director of Public Works and Utilities Ahlen,
Chief of Police Kennedy, Chief of Fire Department Ragusa, Director of Library Services LohGuan,
Director of Human Resources Ko, Management Analyst Alvarez, Deputy Director of Parks and
Recreation Houghton, Economic Development Specialist MacCarley

FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Mayor Maloney

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

SPEAKER, 30 MINUTES TOTAL) – F2M26-4

PRESENTATION

1.  710 PROJECT UPDATES – F2M19-32, F2M20-67

  Assistant City Manager GARCIA delivered a staff report. Consultants Eugene WONG and
  Brandon FRIEDMAN from Kimley-Horn delivered the presentation, which is on file in the City
  Clerk’s office. On October 27, 2025, the City Council requested clarification on the City’s
  overall and project allocation amounts under Measure R 710 Mobility Improvement Project
  (MIP) Funds. In addition, the Council requested a brief summary of the work associated with
  the SB-710 Regional Task Force Planning Committee, which Committee was established
  pursuant to Senate Bill 710 (Durazo) to complete and submit a report to the California
  Legislature on the issues of traffic and potential land uses related to the SR-710 Terminus
  adjacent areas. Staff presented information and updates related to the 710 Project. During the
  presentation, Council asked questions and Mr. Wong and Friedman provided clarification. City
  Manager BINNQUIST also provided clarifications.

  Public Comment:

  The following people expressed concerns regarding the project including funding and
  project timeline:

  1) Ron SAHU, 311 N. Story Pl., also provided written comments which are on file in the City
  Clerk’s office.
  2) Shirley TATSUNO, 1408 S. Fifth St., also requested a public town hall meeting.
  3) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St.
  4) Chris OLSON, N. Curtis Ave., also requested a public town hall meeting.
  5) Melissa MICHELSON
  6) Sawyer BROOKS, 118 E. McLean St., also submitted a handout to Council which is on file
  in the City Clerk’s office, and discussed proposed bike paths as they relate to Alhambra’s
  Bike/Ped Plan.
  7) Curtis CONKIL, via Zoom, also expressed concerns regarding the traffic impact of closing
  the stub.
  8) Marie, via Zoom, also requested a public town hall meeting.
  9) Marisol GRIER, via Zoom, also requested a public town hall meeting.
  10) Raymond QUAN, via Zoom, also expressed concerns regarding the traffic impact of
  closing the stub and requested a public town hall meeting.

  Discussion: Councilmember LEE discussed the background of the project, data collection,
  public input, project timeline, and traffic concerns with Mr. WONG and Mr. FRIEDMAN. Ms.
  LEE, Ms. GARCIA, and City Manager BINNQUIST discussed funding from Measure R.
  Councilmember MAZA, Mr. WONG, and Mr. FRIEDMAN discussed project cost estimates for
  each stage, data collection, the likelihood of obtaining funding from CalTrans, the
  Environmental Impact Report, and traffic concerns and improvements. Mr. MAZA also
  2
2-9-26
   referenced his trip with Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER to Sacramento to secure Alhambra’s portion
  of the stub. Mr. MAZA, Mr. WONG, Mr. FRIEDMAN, and Ms. BINNQUIST also discussed
  competing interests from other stakeholders such as California State University – Los Angeles
  (CalState LA). Mr. MAZA continued to discuss the traffic analyses from METRO and Kimley-
  Horn with the consultants. They also discussed the Advancing Alhambra website and public
  input.

  Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER also referred to her trip with Mr. Maza and further discussed
  the background of the project. She supported a town hall for public input and discussion.

  Councilmember WANG discussed the concerns of the public regarding public input, project
  delays, and transparency. She further discussed traffic concerns and the importance of the
  710 Stub. Ms. WANG, Mr. WONG, and Mr. FRIEDMAN went on to discuss the project timeline
  and the impact of delays on Measure R funds. They also discussed pass through traffic
  statistics and potential ways to address pass through traffic continuing North on Fremont
  Avenue. Ms. WANG, Mr. WONG, Mr. FRIEDMAN, and Mayor MALONEY discussed the EIR
  process. Ms. WANG and the consultants discussed the time in which to select a preferred
  project during the other processes. They also discussed traffic solutions for impacts on other
  City streets during the EIR process. Ms. WANG discussed the issues with the braided ramp.
  She further discussed the funding from Measure R, projected costs, and which alternatives
  could go forward with the consultants. They also discussed the delays with CalTrans and ways
  to potentially move the project along. Ms. WANG discussed her concerns with entering the
  EIR process and the braided ramp. She supported the suggestion for a town hall meeting.

  Mayor MALONEY, Mr. WONG and Mr. FRIEDMAN discussed the current project funding
  allocations. Mr. MALONEY discussed the frustrations with delays from CalTrans, the project
  history and addressed concerns with the EIR process. He also supported the town hall meeting
  after the scoping meeting. Mr. MALONEY and the consultants continued to discuss the project.
  He suggested moving forward on the arterial project and requesting the ability to move forward
  with that process from CalTrans and continued to discuss this with the consultants. They also
  continued to discuss which agency would pay for the EIR, the proposed bike path, updating
  the Advancing Alhambra website, the townhall and scoping meeting for public input, the
  importance of the arterial project, and the need to speed up the project.

  Mr. MAZA reiterated the suggestion to include a method for the public to ask questions and
  get responses via the Advancing Alhambra website and the need to continue conversations
  with CalTrans to partner with the City for funding. Ms. LEE reiterated the need to predict and
  study potential traffic impact on other streets and Mr. FRIEDMAN made clarifications. Ms.
  WANG emphasized the need to conduct the traffic studies before the EIR process. Mr.
  FRIEDMAN and Mr. WONG provided clarification. Ms. WANG also discussed Mr. Maloney’s
  suggestion to continue work on the arterial project and the EIR.

  Council responded to disruptions from the public regarding the need to move to Public
  Comment for Non-Agendized Items.

  Ms. WANG concluded her comments regarding the need for a townhall meeting and the
  scoping for the EIR. She cautioned linking the two. Mr. MALONEY requested staff return to
  the next meeting with more information.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the 710 Project Updates including the
  presentation by Kimley Horn on the City’s 710 Mobility Improvement Projects currently
  underway for the Fremont Avenue On/Off Ramp and the 710 Arterial Conversion (Stub);
  requested staff return with additional information to address concerns.

2.  ACCEPTANCE OF GRANT FUNDS FROM THE LOS ANGELES METROPOLITAN
  TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY UNDER MEASURE R FOR THE 710 STUB
  IMPROVEMENTS INTO A FOUR-LANE ARTERIAL – F2M19-32, M2M26-28

  On April 24, 2023, the City entered into a Cooperative Agreement with the California
  Department of Transportation (Caltrans) for the Project Initiation Document (PID) for the 710
  Stub Improvements at Valley from a six-lane freeway corridor to a four-lane local arterial.
  Featured with the arterial conversion concept are bike lanes, a pedestrian walkway, lighting,
  parkways with trees and landscape, and stormwater pre-treatment elements including water
  capture and reuse elements. On October 10, 2025, the City received the Funding Agreement
  in the amount of $62,400,000 for the City’s Arterial Conversion Project. The funding amounts
  by Fiscal Year are detailed in the February 9, 2026 staff report by the Assistant City Manager.
  The Measure R funds will provide for Project Initiation Document, Project Development,
  Project Approval/Environmental Document, Plans, Specifications, and Estimates, and
  Construction for the City’s Arterial Conversion Project. City Manager BINNQUIST and
  Assistant City Manager GARCIA provided clarification regarding the item.

  Public Comment:  Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., distributed a handout which
  is on file in the City Clerk’s office. He discussed the item and referred to public comment made
  during Item No. 1. He discussed the image referred to by previous comments and which he
  provided to Council.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted grant funds in the amount of $62,400,000 from
  the Los Angeles Metropolitan Transportation Authority under the I-10/SR-710 Interchange
  Reconfiguration (Arterial Conversion), LACMTA Project ID #MR1.1.1.01 and FTIP
  #LAMIPMR123; appropriated $9,000,000 in revenues and expenditures under Measure R for
  the 2024-25, 2025-26 and 2026-27 Fiscal Years, as allocated under the grant; authorized the
  City Manager or designee to execute all documents related to grant implementation; and,
  directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M26-28)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MAZA
  Ayes:  MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, WANG, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

3.  ACCEPT SUMMER LUNCH PROGRAM GRANT FROM THE CALIFORNIA STATE
  LIBRARY AND APPROPRIATE FUNDS – F2M26-18, M2M26-24

  The California State Library offers grants in support of library programs and pop-up visits at
  summer lunch sites to enhance access to books and library services by the community. In
  November, 2025, staff applied for this funding opportunity and was awarded $5,104 to support
  library programming at the City’s park sites participating under the free Summer Lunch

   Program. The grant funds would be used to purchase giveaway books and programming
  supplies to be used during the Library’s mobile visits this summer.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted $5,104 in grant funds from the California State
  Library to support the Library’s mobile summer programs and services; appropriated revenue
  and expenditure funds in the amount of $5,104; authorized the City Manager or designee to
  sign the grant agreement with the California State Library, subject to final language approval
  by the City Manager and City Attorney; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to
  finalize Council’s action. (M2M26-24)

4.  AWARD CONTRACT: ALHAMBRA SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT  SERVICES
  AGREEMENT AUDIT – F2M25-66, RFP2M25-28, C2M26-10, M2M26-25

  On December 8, 2025, the City Council approved staff’s recommendation to solicit proposals
  for professional services to audit the Solid Waste Management Services Agreement with
  Republic Services pursuant to Section 8.2.7 of the Agreement to verify compliance with
  contractual and regulatory requirements. Following Council’s direction, staff issued a Request
  for Proposals (RFP2M25-28) for professional auditing services. Five proposals were received.
  Management Services staff reviewed and scored the proposals based on firm qualifications,
  staffing, schedule, scope of work, and references. HF&H Consultants ranked highest.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a contract, subject to final approval by the City
  Manager and the City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra and HF&H Consultants,
  LLC, for professional services in the amount of $70,000 for a Waste Audit for Rate Year 2023-
  24 under the Solid Waste Management Services Agreement with Republic Services; and,
  directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M26-25)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, WANG, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

5.  RENEWAL OF EDISON EASEMENT LICENSE AGREEMENT – F2M21-30, F2M1-44,
  C2M26-11, M2M26-26

  In 1986, the City of Alhambra entered into a license agreement with SCE to lease the
  easement on Raymond Avenue between Alhambra Road and Cedar Avenue. SCE agreed to
  provide the City with a license to use the property with certain stipulations. Primarily, this would
  involve adequate access for SCE vehicles and employees to maintain their structures and
  non-interference by City improvements with existing power lines or poles. Since the approval
  of the original agreement, the City improved a portion of the property adjacent to Park School,
  by constructing a parking lot, with landscape improvements. This lot has been used by the
  public during the hours Alhambra Park is open. In March 2021, the license agreement was
  5
2-9-26
   renewed for a five-year period, and would expire on March 31, 2026. SCE has offered a five-
  year renewal of the license agreement from April 1, 2026, through March 31, 2031. The license
  agreement would include an annual fee of $581.37 that would increase annually by no more
  than 5%.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the renewal of the license agreement with
  Southern California Edison Company, subject to final language approval by the City Manager
  and City Attorney, for the use of the easement on Raymond Avenue adjacent to Alhambra
  Park for the purpose of park use, for a period of five (5) years, commencing on April 1, 2026
  through March 31, 2031, with an annual fee of $581.37 plus annual increases not to exceed
  5% payable to Southern California Edison; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary
  to finalize Council’s action. (M2M26-26)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY

6.  NOTICE INVITING BIDS: 2026 USDA SUMMER FOOD SERVICE PROGRAM – F2M26-24,
  N2M26-17

  The Summer Food Service Program (SFSP) is a federally funded program administered by
  the State of California Department of Education. The proposed SFSP would begin distributing
  lunches and snacks on June 1, 2026 and would be provided Monday through Friday through
  August 7, 2026. The City would be eligible for reimbursement by the California Department of
  Education for lunches, snacks and operational costs.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the City’s participation in the 2026 Summer
  Food Service Program; authorized staff to circulate a Notice Inviting Bids to secure a vendor
  to provide prepared lunches and snacks for the program; and, directed staff to undertake the
  steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, WANG, MALONEY

8.  NOMINATE AN APPOINTEE FOR METRO SAN GABRIEL VALLEY SERVICE COUNCIL –
  F2M26-16, M2M26-29

  Metro’s Service Councils make decisions about bus routes and schedules for Metro bus lines
  operating in their region. Service Council Bylaws require that nominees live, work, or represent
  the region. Service Council Members may serve more than one three-year term. San Gabriel
  City Council Member John Wu currently serves on behalf of the Cities of Alhambra, San
  Gabriel, San Marino, and South Pasadena as an appointee on Metro’s San Gabriel Valley
  (SGV) Service Council. His term will expire on June 30, 2026. Councilmember Wu was
  appointed to the Council in April 2025. Upon agreement, any one of the four cities may submit
  a letter nominating the incumbent or a replacement candidate to this seat, confirming that there
  is concurrence of all four cities. Metro is requesting that the Cities of Alhambra, San Gabriel,
  San Marino, and South Pasadena submit a nomination to fill the seat for the July 1, 2026 –
  June 30, 2029 term to by April 17, 2026 to ensure that a fully appointed Service Council is
  7
2-9-26
   maintained. Council Member Wu wishes to continue serving on the SGV Service Council and
  the South Pasadena City Council recently took action at their January 21, 2026 meeting to
  approve the continuation of Council Member Wu’s appointment to the SGV Service Council.
  The nomination will be submitted to the Metro Board of Directors at their May 28, 2026 meeting
  for appointment.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council voted to nominate San Gabriel City Council Member John
  Wu as an appointee to the Metro San Gabriel Valley Service Council; and, directed staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M26-29)

11.  CONSIDERATION AND INTRODUCTION FOR FIRST READING OF AN ORDINANCE
  ADOPTING THE PRIMA FACIE SPEED LIMITS IN SCHOOL ZONES IN THE CITY – F2M26-
  7, O2M26-4857

  The recent passage of AB 382 enabled cities to reduce the speed limit in school zones to 20
  miles per hour when children are present. A school zone is defined as an area of 500 feet in
  all directions on the roads adjoining a school. At the January 12, 2026 City Council meeting,
  Councilwoman Adele Andrade-Stadler requested that an item be agendized setting a speed
  8
2-9-26
   limit of 20 miles per hour for the Council’s consideration. The City Council concurred in the
  request. The proposed ordinance would establish a prima facia speed limit of 20 miles per
  hour in school zones when children are present, with the posting of appropriate signage to that
  effect.

  Discussion: Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER thanked staff for the changes to speed limits
  in school zones.

  Action Taken:  City Council declared introduced for its first reading the following
  ordinance entitled:

  Ordinance No. O2M26-4857: An Ordinance of the Alhambra City Council
  adding Section 11.08.075 to Chapter 11.08 of the Alhambra Municipal Code
  establishing a prima facia speed limit of 20 miles per hour in school zones

  which ordinance would return for a second reading and adoption the next regular City Council
  meeting.

COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS (ANNOUNCEMENTS & FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS) – F2M26-7

Mayor MALONEY addressed public comment regarding concerns surrounding Federal Immigration
Enforcement in the City. He referred to previous Resolutions adopted by Council to reaffirm the
Council’s position that the City would not cooperate with Immigration and Customs Enforcement
Officers (ICE) and that the City’s goal is to ensure the protection of residents. He referred to comments
made during Public Comment for Non-Agendized Items and suggested that staff look into ways to
establish “ICE Free Zones” in Alhambra and review similar programs being worked on by Los Angeles
County through signage or other means. He further suggested the formation of a City Council
subcommittee of two, including himself, to review past Resolutions and see how the City is continuing
to work on the standards and goals set forth. Mr. Maloney explained the City’s process to agendize
discussions and the Brown Act. Councilmember MAZA and Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER both
expressed interest in joining the subcommittee. Mr. Maloney suggested that Ms. Andrade-Stadler might
be a more appropriate appointee as the Vice Mayor. Mr. MAZA expressed support for Ms. Andrade-
Stadler and praised her for her past involvement on immigration issues. Mr. MALONEY stated that he
would write a letter of support to the local congressional representatives for the current proposal
currently being discussed in Congress. He urged patience from the community while the City continued
to work for them.

Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER echoed Mr. Maloney’s comments and discussed her involvement
with other organizations such as Unión del Barrio to help immigrant communities. She requested staff
work on a Resolution to address additional concerns. She further discussed recent boycotts of large
businesses such as Home Depot and Target due to concerns with ICE. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER went

 on to address the public speakers concerned with the development at 110 S. Chapel. She requested

Councilmember WANG also addressed speakers concerned with ICE and Federal Immigration

Councilmember MAZA addressed Mr. Ferguson and other public speakers regarding the development
at 110 S. Chapel Ave. and suggested that staff could provide clarification. He addressed public

as well as past Resolutions. Ms. LEE went on to address public speakers regarding the project at 110
